about: The epistle of the First Sunday of Advent, Romans 13:11–14. Saint Paul tells the Romans that the hour has come to rise from sleep, that the night is past and the day at hand, and that they are to put on the Lord Jesus Christ. Fratres, Brethren, is the missal’s own opening for a lesson from an Epistle and is not part of the verse.

seg.tr: Brethren: You know that the hour has now come for us to rise from sleep.

ex.w002: The reading opens with a participle that has no main verb in the Latin: in Paul it continues the appeals of the preceding verses. It describes the people Paul writes to, who know that it is time to rise from sleep. No separate word expresses its subject.

seg.tr: For now our salvation is nearer than when we believed.
The night is past, and the day is at hand.
Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light.

ex.w025: It begins the paired appeal to cast off darkness and put on light.

seg.tr: As in the day, let us walk decently: not in carousing and drunkenness, not in debauchery and wantonness, not in strife and rivalry; but put on the Lord Jesus Christ.
